articles.title: Claressa Shields not upset Katie Taylor fight didn't happen and sends retirement message to Irish great
articles.summary: Claressa Shields and Amanda Serrano both wished Katie Taylor a happy retirement as the Irish great prepares for the final bout of her professional career this weekend; Shields played down the idea she was upset the two never shared the ring, praising Taylor's historic career.
articles.body:
Taylor enters her farewell bout this weekend when she takes on Flora Pili in an undisputed super-lightweight world title clash at Dublin's Croke Park in front of more than 80,000 fans.

The Irish icon, a two-weight undisputed world champion and Olympic gold medallist, will hang up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest fighter in female boxing history.

Five-weight world champion Shields has arguably become the closest rival to Taylor's reputation at the pinnacle of the sport.

"Am I number one? I have always shared that with Katie," Shields told Sky Sports. "Me and her joke and say we're 1A and 1B, because we're both just that good.

"I'm not a person that really cares about the pound for pound list. I know that I've been number one or two on there for the past five, six years.

"But I know that Katie, she's a great fighter. She's a warrior. And I wish her a happy retirement. And I hope that she gets a big knock out her last fight."

Shields, a three-time undisputed world champion, has fought at heavier weight-classes than Taylor, hence the pair never crossing paths in their respective glittering careers.

"I'm not mad that it didn't happen," said Shields. "We had weight classes for a reason. And I respect her greatness and she respects mine.

"I beat the best in my divisions, and she's beat the best in her divisions. I respect that. So no, I'm not upset that we never got to fight.

"I am happy to be able to watch her and her greatness. She's done the same for me. And like I said, I wish her a happy retirement."

Taylor enters Saturday's contest 25-1 having suffered her only professional career defeat against Chantelle Cameron in May 2023.

Among her highlights is a trilogy of wins over Puerto Rican great Amanda Serrano, the first of which saw the pair compete in the first ever women's boxing match to headline at Madison Square Garden.

"I think Katie's done what she wanted to do. I think this is her time," Serrano told Sky Sports.

"You can feel it, I've been 17 years in the sport. It's about time.

"Me and Katie, we've made lots of money together, we made history together and big fights. I think she's done enough for the sport. She deserves this homecoming fight.

"I'm happy for her. I just can't wait to see her future when she's retired with her family life and all that good stuff. She deserves it."

articles.title: Coach Hints at Islam Makhachev’s Potential UFC Return Date
articles.summary: American Kickboxing Academy head coach Javier Mendez hinted at when UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev will be ready to fight again.Makhachev is comin...
articles.body:
American Kickboxing Academy head coach Javier Mendez hinted at when UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev will be ready to fight again.

Makhachev is coming off a unanimous decision win over Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330 that saw him pick up his 17th win in a row, which is a UFC record.

That was Makhachev's only fight so far in 2026, but his coach says he might fight one more time before the year is up.

Islam Makhachev Could Return in December

Speaking on the "Weighing In" podcast, Mendez said that Makhachev could return tot the Octagon in December at UFC 335 if the promotion gives him enough notice so he can have a full two-month training camp.

"I think that he could be ready December on up potentiall. Potentially because I don't know exactly where his mind is at but one thing I do know, Islam's not gonna say no to any opponent. His only issue is going to be when do they want him to fight and that's it. The date (and) if he can have enough time because he always wants two months training camp. He's not going to take six weeks, seven weeks. Islam wants a two month training camp," Mendez said (via Bloody Elbow ).

As for who Makhachev will fight next, ultimately, it's the UFC's call who they will match him up against. But by all indications, it will be Carlos Prates, the Brazilian knockout artist who is confident that he can be the man who ends Makhachev's long UFC win streak.

If the UFC can get the fight booked, then Makhachev vs. Prates would be a terrific headliner for UFC 335, which takes place in December in Las Vegas.

There have been suggestions that UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland could headline that card, but as of right now, Strickland has not been cleared to fight again following a shoulder injury he suffered before his fight against Khamzat Chimaev at UFC 328.

articles.title: UFC Champion Pulls Out Of UFC 332, Promotion Scrambles To Replace Main Event
articles.summary: Valentina Shevchenko is out of UFC 332 with an injury. Natalia Silva vs. Wang Cong for the interim flyweight title is reportedly being worked on for Oct. 3.
articles.body:
The UFC 332 has been thrown into a state of flux. UFC women's flyweight champion Valentina Shevchenko has been forced off the card with an injury. She was set to defend her 125-pound title against top contender Natalia Silva. With the champion out, the card's main event has been all but ruined. However, UFC brass is scrambling to find a replacement to ensure a title fight remains on the card. And they may have found a replacement for Shevchenko. Let's talk MMA.

Valentina Shevchenko vs. Natalia Silva, women's flyweight title

Shevchenko out with an undisclosed injury

Natalia Silva vs. Wang Cong, interim women's flyweight title

None. Dana White said the main event would be announced this week

Wang beat Shevchenko in a 2015 kickboxing bout

The injury report came from Brazilian outlet Ag. Fight , and the UFC has since removed Shevchenko vs. Silva from its website . Neither the promotion nor Shevchenko has commented publicly.

The interim booking traces to a single account on X and remains unannounced. UFC CEO Dana White said after Tuesday's Contender Series that the main event would be named this week.

Wang Cong has been on a roll with four straight wins after suffering the only loss of her MMA career to Gabriella Fernandes in November 2024. Most recently, Wang defeated Tracy Cortez via unanimous decision in July. The win pushed Wang to No. 6 in the flyweight division. Elevating her into a No. 1 contender or interim title fight with Silva makes sense. The other contenders ahead of Wang and behind Silva have either already had their shot at the title (Manon Fiorot, Alexa Grasso, Zhang Weili) or are sidelined and unavailable for the date (Erin Blanchfield).

For casual fans, Shevchenko-Silva was a weak main event on paper. Wang-Silva for an interim title reads even weaker to the average fan. The hardcores will still have some interest because the matchup still represents highly skilled, top-of-the-line mixed martial artists.

articles.title: Taylor-Pili: 'You couldn't make Katie Taylor's story up' - Eddie Hearn
articles.summary: Promoter Eddie Hearn says "the whole story, you couldn't make it up", when speaking of Katie Taylor's journey.
articles.body:
As promoter Eddie Hearn tries to quantify the impact Katie Taylor has made throughout her career, there is a smile and shake of the head as he says, "the whole story, you couldn't make it up."

On Saturday night, Taylor will make her final walk to the ring when she takes on Flora Pili at Croke Park, with the chance to become undisputed light-welterweight champion once again.

While Taylor entered professional boxing in 2016 with an Olympic gold medal, five world and seven European amateur titles to her name, there were no guarantees that star power could flourish in the paid code where women's boxing remained firmly in the shadows.

After agreeing to meet Taylor, her mother Bridget and manager Brian Peters, Hearn's interest was more than piqued.

"I went into that meeting, I would say 90% in my mind I wasn't going to do anything," said the Matchroom chairman.

"She's so fierce and the way she was talking, like the passion, the determination and she was telling me the story about the Olympics [pushing for women's boxing to be added to the programme for London 2012] and I was just like, 'this is unbelievable'. That was when we decided to headline her in November."

The decision to put Taylor on after Ohara Davies' victory over Andrea Scarpa that night at Wembley Arena was met with some scepticism from his father, Barry.

"He's like, 'oh, mate, no one's interested in the women's boxing' but he watched her debut and he was like, 'oh my God'.

"From there, the story's been unbelievable."

Taylor made around £6000 for that initial victory, "at the time in women's boxing, a lot of money" Hearn reflected, but that proved yet another obstacle Taylor was determined to overcome for female fighters.

Following a defence of the WBA and IBF light weight titles against Cindy Serrano - sister of great rival Amanda - at Boston's TD Garden in 2018, Taylor questioned why Tevin Farmer, who defended his IBF super-featherweight title against James Tennyson on the same card, made significantly more money.

"She said, 'do you think that's fair?', and I was like, 'no, but I just think that's the world and where we are right now'," Hearn recounted.

"She's like, 'well, how can I sell more tickets, how can more people be interested in me, how can more people want to tune in to watch me fight, yet he's making three times as much?'. I said, 'because he's a man and that's what you need to change'.

"Now she's making more than 99% of male fighters out there."

The three fights with Amanda Serrano, two at a sold-out Madison Square Garden and another on the Jake Paul-Mike Tyson card in Texas, have helped transform career earnings and raise the profile for women's boxing to heights many could not have envisaged.

While Taylor again pushed her promoter to seek a higher purse than the "incredible" offer made by Paul's MVP for that second meeting, Hearn accepts "she was right" and despite fighter and promoter not having a contract "for years and years", he can only conclude the Bray woman has been "incredible to work with".

The love and respect for the 40-year-old has been evident in the build-up to Saturday's last dance with contemporaries, former opponents and many more outside the boxing bubble lining up to show their appreciation for a career that has transformed the female fight game.

"Boxing is a really toxic world," Hearn accepts.

"There's always people who don't like people but there isn't one female fighter you could find that wouldn't go, 'she's incredible'.

"She's just so loved, there's no airs or graces. She's not there for the fame, she's not there for the money, it's purely her faith, the love of the sport and trying to set an example."

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili: 'How far we have come' - Deirdre Gogarty writes back to Katie Taylor
articles.summary: Ireland's first female world champion writes a letter to Katie Taylor, 30 years after receiving one from her.
articles.body:
Before Deirdre Gogarty became Ireland's first female world boxing champion in 1997, she had already inspired a young Irish girl.

A 10-year-old Katie Taylor wrote to her hero in 1996 saying she did not "see boxing for girls taking off here", adding "maybe one day they'll even let us box in the Olympics". As Taylor is set to retire on Saturday as one of Ireland's greatest sportspeople, Gogarty writes back to the 40-year-old...

As I prepare to come home to Ireland to watch you fight at Croke Park, I keep thinking about just how far we have come.

It has been 39 years since I first walked through the doors of a boxing gym in Drogheda and was finally allowed to train.

Back then, I was told women would never be accepted in boxing. That even if we were allowed to compete, nobody would want to watch.

There was a time when I would have given anything simply to be allowed into a ring. We fought in places with few spectators, little recognition, and almost no opportunities for women.

And now, tens of thousands of people will fill one of Ireland's most iconic sporting venues to watch two women box... wow!!!

What was once considered unacceptable has become something an entire nation celebrates.

Katie, what you have done for women's boxing goes far beyond championships, medals, and records.

You didn't simply succeed in the sport - you helped transform how the world sees it, so that another generation of girls never has to question whether they belong.

When I sit among that enormous crowd at Croke Park, I'll be thinking about all the women who fought when nobody was watching.

I'll be thinking about the girls who were told they couldn't and shouldn't.

And most of all, I'll be thinking about the young girls watching you who will never have to ask permission to dream.

Thank you for writing to me and sending me you profile. Sorry I couldn't get back to you sooner as I was doing school exams. I train two nights a week up in my da's club. My da is having his own show in January and he is looking for a fight for me.

I am fed up not being to get fights especially when I see the lads I spar winning championships. There is the European championships for women being held in Sweden in May and my da is trying to enter me into them.

There is an open championship being held in England in April and hopefully I'll be entering that as well. I will let you know how I get on. Sorry to hear your fight in January is looking doubtful (Paddy was telling us).

I hope you can get it on. Hopefully if you get a fight in Ireland, we will all come and see you. My brother Peter recently won the Leinster nine counties and is the reigning champion of the Wicklow/Wexford championship and is fighting in the finals of them again in January on my da's show.

It will be a tough one as his opponent is the All-Ireland champion. I can't see boxing for girls taking off over here in the near future. I can see why you had to go away to get fights.

Hopefully things will change over the next few years but maybe one day they'll even let us box in the Olympics. I hope everything goes well with your boxing career. You have achieved so much already, you have done us all proud. I wish you continued success.

(Tell Christy Martin I'm getting ready for her ha ha)

articles.title: La increíble historia de Michael Aljarouj, el rival de Fabià Sintes en UFC París
articles.standfirst: El peleador francés ha tenido una vida muy difícil marcada por intentos de secuestro y una guerra civil en Siria que han forjado su carácter
articles.summary: El peleador francés ha tenido una vida muy difícil marcada por intentos de secuestro y una guerra civil en Siria que han forjado su carácter
articles.body: Este sábado 5 de septiembre, Fabià Sintes (11-3) tendrá la oportunidad de su vida en el UFC París, donde debutará en la promotora de MMA más importante del mundo ante Michael Aljarouj (13-3, 2NC). Ambos son de los mayores prospectos de peso mosca a nivel europeo, y el peleador galo tiene una historia de superación detrás marcada por una guerra civil, un intento de secuestro y una huida a Francia que le salvó la vida y le permitió saltar al estrellato en los deportes de contacto. A nivel deportivo, Aljarouj es un finalizador nato, con un porcentaje de finalización del 77%, algo inusual para un peso mosca donde la mayoría de los combates suelen ir a puntos. El galo llega con el cartel de campeón de peso mosca de Hexagone, aunque su último combate ante Romero Dos Reis tuvo cierta polémica, ya que perdió por decisión pero finalmente se corrigió el resultado a un 'No Contest'. Al igual que Fabià, el récord de Aljarouj está marcado por sus inicios profesionales, donde sumó dos derrotas en sus primeras seis peleas. A partir de ahí comenzó a ganar y a finalizar a sus oponentes, y este sábado en el Accor Arena será el ídolo local que intente entrar con buen pie en la UFC ante el actual campeón de peso mosca de WOW FC. Según él mismo, el peleador español ya rechazó un combate entre ambos hace unos meses, por lo que este sábado resolverán sus cuentas pendientes. Sin embargo, lo que más llama la atención de Aljarouj no es su carrera profesional, sino su historia de superación desde que era muy joven. Nació en Alepo -Siria- en 1997, y con 14 años vivió una guerra civil que le obligó a sufrir la crueldad de las bombas cayendo en su territorio mientras iba al instituto. Ahí entró en juego su conocimiento de las artes marciales mixtas, ya que desde pequeño sus padres le apuntaron a deportes de contacto para que pudiese defenderse en un futuro. Desgraciadamente tuvo que usarlo de la peor manera posible, ya que le intentaron secuestrar y meterlo dentro de un coche amenazándole con un cuchillo. Sin embargo, Aljarouj no se puso nervioso, se lo arrebató al secuestrador y se lo clavó en la pierna para poder escapar. Esto fue uno de los detonantes para que sus padres decidiesen que era hora de emigrar, aunque todavía quedaba lo peor. En un autobús rumbo a Líbano, un grupo de terroristas interceptaron el vehículo y consideraron que Michael era el sujeto perfecto para incorporarlo a sus filas. Sin embargo, en un acto de valentía su padre les ofreció cualquier cosa para poder salvarle de esa situación, y acabó pagando una gran cantidad de dinero para salvar a su hijo. En ese momento el plan de ir al Líbano pasó a ser una huida a Francia, donde se reuniría con sus padres poco tiempo después. A partir de ahi comenzó su carrera en las MMA hasta hoy. Un peleador que no tiene miedo al subirse al octágono porque ya le ha tocado vivir historias de todo tipo, y este sábado será el encargado de dar la bienvenida a Fabià Sintes a la UFC.

articles.title: Movsar Evloev eyes 26-pound weight cut as he opens up on UFC lightweight move following Alexander Volkanovski featherweight title fight at UFC 333
articles.summary: MMA News: Movsar Evloev is preparing for the biggest fight of his UFC career. The undefeated Russian will challenge Alexander Volkanovski for the featherweight .
articles.body: Movsar Evloev is preparing for the biggest fight of his UFC career. The undefeated Russian will challenge Alexander Volkanovski for the featherweight title at UFC 333 next month. Evloev has earned his first UFC title shot after winning 10 straight fights inside the Octagon.However, the featherweight contender is already thinking about his future beyond the title fight. Evloev admitted that making the 145-pound limit is becoming increasingly difficult. The Russian said he is getting bigger and may eventually have to move up to lightweight. He revealed that he currently needs to cut around 26 pounds to compete at featherweight.Movsar Evloev admits featherweight weight cut is becoming harderMovsar Evloev has established himself as one of the UFC’s most difficult featherweights to beat. He remains undefeated and has built an impressive winning run inside the promotion.His reward is a title opportunity against Volkanovski. The Australian champion has spent years competing at the highest level. Volkanovski has also suggested that UFC 333 could potentially be his final fight if the contest leaves him badly hurt.Evloev recently caused confusion when he appeared to agree with Volkanovski’s comments about retirement. He later explained that his comment did not mean he was planning to retire.Instead, the Russian wanted to make it clear that his focus is on winning. He does not intend to walk away simply because his opponent has retirement plans.While retirement is not currently on Evloev’s mind, a move to another division could eventually become necessary.The 31-year-old discussed his future during an appearance on The Bohnfire. He was asked about the possibility of moving to lightweight, particularly after former opponent Diego Lopes was linked with a move up.Evloev admitted that he has also considered making the jump.His main concern is the physical demand of remaining at featherweight. The Russian explained that he is naturally getting bigger. As a result, the weight cut is becoming more difficult.“I’m getting bigger every day so one day, I don’t know how long it will take, one day I need to move up because now I need to cut about 26 pounds to be featherweight,” he said.Evloev did not give a specific timeline for when he could move to lightweight. His immediate priority remains his title fight with Volkanovski.A victory would make Evloev the UFC featherweight champion and could give him more flexibility when deciding his long-term future.Volkanovski, meanwhile, will enter the fight with plenty of experience in championship contests. His coach Joe Lopez also believes the Australian could struggle to walk away even if he loses.“We’ll discuss it with him obviously and go through it but knowing Alex, if he loses, he’ll go, ‘I don’t want to go out on a loss and I want to come back and get it back. Come back on a win.’ I just know how competitive he is,” Lopez said.For now, Evloev’s attention remains on the biggest challenge of his career. But his comments suggest that lightweight could eventually be part of his UFC future.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili: Paddy Donovan won't 'underestimate' Tyrone McKenna in Croke Park undercard bout
articles.summary: Paddy Donovan insists he is not "underestimating" Tyrone McKenna before they meet at Croke Park on Saturday with a second crack at world honours on the horizon.
articles.body:
Paddy Donovan insists he is not "underestimating" Tyrone McKenna before they meet at Croke Park on Saturday with a second crack at world honours on the horizon.

Donovan bounced back from his first title defeat by Lewis Crocker with an impressive victory over Karen Chukhadzhian in May to return to the mandatory slot for the IBF welterweight title held by Australia's Liam Paro.

The Limerick man is aware of the risks in taking a fight in the interim, but felt this was too good an opportunity to turn down and plans to put on a show to elevate his status.

He and McKenna have sparred countless rounds over the years and the 27-year-old, whose record is 15 wins with two defeats, feels he is a level above his fellow southpaw.

"It's risky to take the fight being number one with the IBF but I couldn't turn down the opportunity to fight in front of 80,000 Irish fans," Donovan said at Thursday's news conference.

"We want to bring big shows back to Ireland when Katie's gone and I'm going to be the guy to do it.

"I'm not underestimating you [McKenna], I've a job to do so I'll beat you and move onto becoming a world champion, but you're first and I'll deal with you good and proper."

'You couldn't make Taylor's story up' - Hearn

Taylor prepared for test rather than testimonial

'Dear Katie, how far we have come...' - Taylor gets reply from her hero

Veteran McKenna [25-6-1] has lost two of his last four fights after reversing a decision to retire following his own defeat by Crocker in 2023.

However, the Belfast man is not content to play the role of gatekeeper and set up camp in Philadelphia - where he spent an early part of his career - to work in 'The Dungeon' gym of Derrick 'Bozy' Ennis - father of undefeated two-division champion Jaron 'Boots'.

"To bring a west Belfast man to north Philly is a dangerous combination," said the 36-year-old.

"This is the most I've sparred in a camp, in a world-class gym surrounded by world champions and world-class fighters. The coaching has been world-class, so I've done everything for this fight.

"I think Paddy is overlooking me as all I hear is 'Liam Paro, Lewis Crocker', but you [Donovan] have to get your mind right because I'm coming for you."

Chief support on Saturday is a heavyweight contest between Dave Allen [27-9-2] and Thomas Carty [11-1].

Doncaster's Allen admits his ambitions of fighting for top honours are over following May's defeat by newly-crowned IBF heavyweight champion Filip Hrgovic.

However, he has bounced back with a pair of routine wins and feels he remains a "proper handful" at his level.

"After the Hrgovic fight, all of the feeling for boxing left me," the 34-year-old revealed.

"I'm not trying to resurrect any run for titles, I'm just here to fight but if you're not very good, I'll flatten you."

Carty once had aspirations to play Gaelic football for Dublin at Croke Park, but on Saturday he will realise something of a dream when boxing at the home of the Gaelic Athletic Association.

His sole defeat came at Madison Square Garden in March 2025 when suffering an ACL injury against Dajuan Calloway, but the 30-year-old southpaw feels he is "probably better now than what I was before" the injury.

Another Dubliner, Emmet Brennan, will make the 500-metre journey from his house to Croke Park to face fellow unbeaten super-middleweight Taylor Bevan with added incentive of double pay by Brian Peters, who represents Bevan, should he prevail.

Meanwhile, MMA convert Molly McCann continues her boxing journey against Sylwia Doligala.

McCann, who has won all four of her bouts since making the switch to professional boxing, is a relative of headliner Katie Taylor with her late grandmother a great-aunt of the Bray woman - and she recounted her own early struggles to find acceptance in the boxing world.

"I remember walking into a boxing gym and was turned away as I was a girl," said the 36-year-old Liverpudlian.

"[I] then started boxing at the Golden Gloves gym and my coach brought in a camcorder, told me to watch this girl and lo and behold, it was Katie.

"I was like 'oh my God, I want to be like that', and 20 years later here we are. It's not lost on me how many girls would kill to be in this position, so it's an honour and privilege."

articles.title: Khamzat Chimaev accepts surprising fight offer from top UFC contender after losing middleweight title
articles.summary: International Sports News: Khamzat Chimaev could already have his next UFC opponent lined up. The former middleweight champion has appeared open to a fight with Caio Borralho, w.
articles.body: Khamzat Chimaev could already have his next UFC opponent lined up. The former middleweight champion has appeared open to a fight with Caio Borralho, who recently called for the matchup and offered two possible dates for the showdown. If it happens, the fight would mark Chimaev’s first appearance since losing his title to Sean Strickland at UFC 328. The matchup would also give both fighters plenty to fight for. Borralho is currently No. 6 in the Meta UFC middleweight rankings, while Chimaev remains the UFC’s No. 12 pound-for-pound fighter. More importantly, both men are coming from very different points in their careers, with Borralho pushing toward the title picture and Chimaev trying to get back to the belt.Caio Borralho puts UFC 334 and UFC 335 on the tableBorralho made his intentions pretty clear after Chimaev recently mentioned possible opponents on social media. The Brazilian contender quickly jumped at the opportunity and directly called for the former champion.“Finally someone called my name! My brother u know I love you, and I’m ready MSG November or T Mobile December! Just let me know,” Borralho wrote.That gives the UFC two obvious options if the promotion decides to book the fight. UFC 334 is scheduled for Madison Square Garden, while UFC 335 will take place at T-Mobile Arena. They are also set to be the final two major UFC cards of 2026.Borralho has a reason to believe he belongs in that conversation. He started his UFC run with seven straight wins before losing a decision to Nassourdine Imavov at UFC Paris last year. He bounced back at UFC 326, defeating Reinier de Ridder by unanimous decision.Chimaev’s plans have changed since the title lossThe biggest twist is what Chimaev originally said after his defeat.Following the split-decision loss to Strickland, Chimaev indicated that he planned to move up to light heavyweight. That plan now appears to have changed. At 32, he instead seems interested in staying at middleweight and making another run toward the championship.A fight against Borralho would fit that route. It wouldn't be an immediate rematch with Strickland, but it could put Chimaev back into the contender mix while giving Borralho a huge opportunity at 185 pounds.There is also a separate question hanging over the division: who gets the next title shot if Chimaev fights Borralho?Who could challenge Sean Strickland next?Nassourdine Imavov currently sits at No. 3 in the Meta UFC middleweight rankings and owns five straight wins. His latest victory came against Borralho, while his earlier career includes a short-notice loss to Strickland in 2023.Dricus du Plessis is ranked No. 2 and already has two wins over Strickland, making him another obvious name in the title picture. Then there’s Joe Pyfer at No. 4, who stopped Israel Adesanya at UFC Seattle in March.So, if Chimaev and Borralho do meet, the middleweight title picture could take another turn. For now, Borralho is preparing for “big news” this month, while Chimaev appears willing to answer his call.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Gaethje ya no quiere vengarse de Holloway y Oliveira: "Como Topuria los venció..."
articles.standfirst: El campeón de peso ligero cree que su victoria ante 'El Matador' le vale como redención de las dos derrotas más dolorosas de su carrera
articles.summary: El campeón de peso ligero cree que su victoria ante 'El Matador' le vale como redención de las dos derrotas más dolorosas de su carrera
articles.body: Justin Gaethje está viviendo la mejor época de su carrera con 37 años. Desde que ganase a Ilia Topuria en el UFC Casa Blanca del pasado 14 de junio, el peleador estadounidense ha cumplido todos los sueños que tenía en su carrera, e incluso ha afirmado que ya no tiene intención de vengarse de sus dos derrotas más dolorosas: la de Max Holloway y la de Charles Oliveira. Contra Oliveira peleó por el cinturón de peso ligero en 2022, y después de un primer asalto frenético en el que estuvo a punto de finalizar a 'Do Bronx' acabó siendo sometido, perdiendo la oportunidad de su vida de ser campeón indiscutido. Un golpe muy duro para su carrera teniendo en cuenta que el brasileño falló el peso y él era el único que podía salir campeón de ese combate. Aun así, 'The Highlight' se repuso y siguió intentándolo, e incluso noqueó a Dustin Poirier de una patada a la cabeza para redimirse del primer enfrentamiento entre ambos y convertirse en campeón BMF, lo que le volvía a acercar a la oportunidad titular. Sin embargo, antes de eso tuvo que medirse a Max Holloway en el UFC 300, donde una patada giratoria le rompió la nariz al final del primer asalto y a falta de un segundo para finalizar la pelea fue víctima de uno de los mejores K.O. de la historia de la UFC. De nuevo, Justin se levantó y siguió ganando combates, y cuando parecía que todo estaba perdido arrasó a Paddy Pimblett el pasado enero para convertirse en campeón interino y a Topuria para ser por fin campeón indiscutido. Como 'El Matador' ya noqueó a Holloway y Oliveira, Gaethje considera que ya no tiene necesidad de vengarse. De hecho, quiere pelear contra Conor McGregor para sumar otro nombre a su colección. “Hubiera tenido una revancha con Oliveira o Holloway, pero como Topuria los venció, voy a justificarme diciéndome que ya me desquité de ellos. Entonces supongo que McGregor, sería divertido callarlo", afirmó a UFC con Paramount. Con McGregor parece complicado que se enfrente por el hecho de que el irlandés viene de romperse el ligamento cruzado de la rodilla derecha en su pelea contra Max Holloway y si vuelve será en la International Flight Week de junio de 2027 contra un rival más asequible que el tipo más en forma de la división. Además, Conor está peleando actualmente en peso wélter, y se antoja muy complicado que vuelva a bajar de división después de todo lo que ha pasado. Además, Gaethje tampoco quiere darle la revancha a Topuria al creer que no ha hecho méritos suficientes tras ser finalizado. Por tanto, el escenario para el peleador estadounidense pasa por enfrentarse a otros retadores como Arman Tsarukyan, aunque no le deben de quedar más de una o dos peleas en la recámara. De hecho, 'The Highlight' ya reconoció hace unos combates que en el momento en el que perdiese se retiraría, y ahora que ha cumplido su sueño ese fin de carrera está más cerca que nunca. Por tanto, Topuria tiene complicado poder vengarse de esa derrota tras las negativas de Gaethje, aunque es la UFC la que tiene la última palabra.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Mayor of London Sadiq Khan issues plea to Eddie Hearn and Frank Warren to 'get fight to London'
articles.summary: The Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, has urged promoters to get Fury vs AJ to London; Khan revealed that he was approached by Eddie Hearn for help with organising the fight; Sky Sports has approached Queensbury Boxing and Matchroom Promotions for comment
articles.body:
Fury and Joshua had just days ago appeared closer than ever to agreeing a super-fight long-in-the-making, only for Saudi organisers Sela's wish to hold the event in the USA to emerge as a major stumbling block.

While Joshua's side have maintained their desire for the fight to take place in the UK, Fury branded his potential opponent a "coward" on social media earlier this week, questioning the hold up in agreeing final terms to the fight, with his promoter Frank Warren asserting Fury had signed his side of the deal.

Khan, though, has issued a plea for organisers to satisfy the desires of the fighters themselves and stage the fight in London.

"I understand the temptation of going to Madison Square Gardens," Khan told Sky Sports News. "I understand the temptation of the money and offer, but the fans are here.

"We've been loyal to Tyson and to Anthony. We love them both, and we'd love to see them boxing here in London.

"I'm positive Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua know how much we love both of them. I'm not sure how much the promoters know how much we love both of them, but my message to the promoters is why don't you do what Tyson and Anthony want, which is get the fight in London.

"We'll get 100,000 people watching them live, plus millions watching across the globe fighting amongst the fans who've loved them from the beginning."

Khan also revealed he had been in direct contact with Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn, saying the Matchroom chairman had approached him for help with organising the fight:

"We've hosted some of the biggest boxing events in history in London during my mayoralty.

"Many British fans are fans of Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Many Londoners love both Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Both Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua recognise the importance of British boxing fans.

"The promoters know we're here to help. We've approached those in the know to say we're here to help.

"Eddie Hearn has approached us and we're keen to work with Eddie and the team."

Sky Sports has approached Queensbury Boxing and Matchroom Promotions for comment.

articles.title: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury: London mayor Sadiq Khan wants fight at Wembley
articles.summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan says he is "really keen" to host the proposed Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium and has urged promoters to get in touch.
articles.body:
London Mayor Sadiq Khan says he is "really keen" to host the proposed Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium and has urged promoters to get in touch.

BBC Sport understands Saudi organisers Sela have contacted the mayor's office in recent weeks about bringing the long-awaited contest to the national stadium.

However, with organisers and broadcaster Netflix understood to favour New York's Madison Square Garden for a November bout, sources close to the discussions say talks over a London venue have not progressed, with no detailed talks over dates or timings.

"A message to the promoters - we want to host it in London. Talk to us, we're really keen to have it," Khan told BBC Sport on Thursday.

Wembley Stadium's usual curfew is 23:00, although Khan has previously indicated he would support efforts to bring the fight to London.

A late-night fight in London - potentially in the early hours - could mean it draws a larger television audience in the US.

Brent Council, the local authority involved in any approval, has said a potential extension of the curfew would need to be assessed by Wembley's safety advisory group.

It remains unclear how late that curfew could be pushed back.

"Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are two great British boxers. Both have been world champions," Khan said.

"They both recognise and love the fans in this country who have supported them throughout their careers, amateur and professional.

"Wembley has hosted many fantastic events, including bouts involving Tyson and Anthony. We, the fans, want to see them box live in London."

There is hope that the venue will be finalised in the coming days. Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has said he wants an announcement this week, with a news conference to follow next week.

BBC Sport has contacted Sela for comment.

Fury calls Joshua a 'coward' as wait for announcement continues

Hearn says his side signed a contract for the bout to take place in the United Kingdom, while Sela and Netflix's preference would be the United States, to cater for American audiences.

Matchroom Boxing's Hearn has previously said Joshua's contract specifically stipulated a UK venue and would need to be renegotiated for the fight to take place Stateside.

Hearn says he has since set out terms under which Matchroom would agree to the change, with negotiations continuing over a possible move to New York.

The contact from Sela represents a significant development from the end of July, when sources close to the mayor told BBC Sport there had been no approach from the fight's organisers.

But the lack of progress since that initial contact underlines the uncertainty still surrounding Wembley's chances of hosting the contest.

"I'm hoping the promoters understand that not only will you get 100,000 people watching this bout live, you'll get millions watching it across the globe, where both boxers are cheered on by their loyal fans," Khan said.

articles.title: Mailbag: UFC 332 is looking like an event without a headliner, and time is running out
articles.summary: Why is UFC 332 still without a main event just one month out from the event? And how concerned should we be about Bella Mir's comments on her father's brain...
articles.body:
UFC 332 lost its title fight and is in dire need of some help to fill out the fight card with just a month left to go, so what gives? Plus, Bella Mir says her former UFC champion father's brain is "not good today" after all the punishment of a long career. How concerned should the MMA world be about that?

All that and more in this week's mailbag. To ask a question of your own, hit up @BenFowlkesMMA on X or @Ben_Fowlkes on Threads.

@michal_sobek: UFC332 is 30 days away, with no main event and an underwhelming card. Utah is paying to bring UFC there. Is this what they had in mind with the deal?Compared to UFC 333, the contrast is crazy. Do you think fighters avoid Utah due to altitude, and that's why the card is like this?

If fighters were that scared of the elevation then Mexico City and Denver would never get any decent fights. I've talked to a bunch of fighters about this over the years and you would be absolutely stunned by how many of them just don't know or care when they're accepting fights at higher elevations. They're way more likely to avoid certain spots for tax purposes (especially if they've had their money yanked there once already) than they are to think that thin air could possibly affect a beast like them.

But you're not wrong about UFC 332 looking like a glorified Fight Night event right now. I keep seeing rumors that it will be headlined by an interim title bout between Natalia Silva and Wang Cong, but I refuse to believe it. Maybe I just don't want to believe it, since that would essentially mean the UFC has decided that it doesn't have to try at all anymore.

I'm glad you made the point about Salt Lake City paying to bring the UFC to town, though. That helps explain how we got here. Right now UFC 332 has no main event and only one fight featuring ranked fighters (No. 9 Deiveson Figueiredo vs. No. 11 Payton Talbott). It's listed as UFC 332: TBD vs. TBD" on the UFC website. Tickets are on sale and plenty of good seats are still available. So why isn't there some urgency about bolstering this event that's a month away?

The answer is because the UFC gets paid either way. It gets paid by Salt Lake City whether anyone shows up or not. And it gets paid by Paramount+ whether anyone watches or not. Good for the suits at TKO, who have figured out a way to remove the UFC from its own historical incentive structure and still make money. Not so good for the fans.

@jaypettry: Have you listened to the new Mastodon album? It absolutely rips, and it's an unexpected tearjerker too. Oh, about MMA? What do you posit is the best possible, realistic, sellable headliner you could matchmake for UFC 332 one month away?

@jaypettry: Have you listened to the new Mastodon album? It absolutely rips, and it's an unexpected tearjerker too.

Oh, about MMA? What do you posit is the best possible, realistic, sellable headliner you could matchmake for UFC 332 one month away?

It's the whole one-month-away thing that's really a problem. No one with an actual UFC title should be willing to risk it on that kind of notice. Not unless they were already dialed in and going hard in the gym. So that leaves something like a just-for-fun brawl between big names as the best possible option.

Who fits that description? There's a handful we could name. But who's available and willing at this late hour? That's the part only the UFC matchmakers know for sure. And man, I hope they're on the phone right now trying to talk those people into it. This card needs something and it needs it soon.

@Beastin364: Did you see the part of Bella Mir's interview on Ariel's show where she said her dad is dealing with lots of brain damage now? First I've heard of Frank having those issues and seems like a big deal that people are sorta shrugging off

That was concerning, to say the least. But it reminds me of something I've been saying for a while now, which is that we don't know what an elderly MMA fighter looks like yet. The sport hasn't been around long enough.

The pioneers who broke in just as the sport was gaining enough momentum for this to be a somewhat regular gig — guys like Don Frye, Randy Couture, Mark Coleman — are just now getting into their 60s. Guys like Frank Mir were the next generation, the first to enter this sport as young men and stick with it as a full-time lifestyle.

Mir fought for about 18 years, pretty much all of it at the UFC (and Bellator) level. He took a lot of damage but not an uncommon amount. He probably sparred hard and not all that smart, as most of that generation did. It might be more surprising if he didn't have some brain trauma, not to mention the wear and tear on the joints.

The point is, I know people get sick of those of us in the media who harp on fighter pay. But this is why. There is a cost to doing this sport. There are ways to mitigate it, and a lot of younger fighters are much better about doing that. But you're never going to remove entirely the physical toll that fighting for a living takes on a person. They should at least be paid fairly for it, and ideally have some kind of pension or ongoing health care set up by the promoters who profited from their self-destruction.

@MMAMATLOCK: Did you pre-order Cory Sandhagen's comic book? When can we expect a full review?

I'll be honest, this is the first I'm hearing about " Gnos and the Dervies ," by Cory Sandhagen, but I'm absolutely interested. Any fighter who sits down and writes a whole book in between battles inside the cage deserves our support.

Jon Jones. While I still don't believe he's retired, his story would be wild and weird and maybe even weirdly tragic. In a lot of ways he's the most supremely talented fighter in the history of the sport. If someone could ever get the whole truth and nothing but truth from his friends and family and training partners and coaches, man, it would be a wild ride. But I'm not holding my breath on that one.

articles.title: Taylor-Pili: How does the referee prepare for Saturday's world title fight at Croke Park?
articles.summary: Belfast's David Irving tells BBC Sport NI that being the man in the middle for Saturday's world title fight against Flora Pili will represent the fulfilment of a dream.
articles.body:
When Katie Taylor steps into the ring at Croke Park in front of 80,000 fans for her world title fight with Flora Pili on Saturday night it will not just represent the fulfilment of a dream for the legendary Irish boxer.

For Belfast referee David Irving, who will be the man in the middle for the 27th and final professional bout of Taylor's decorated career, it will also be the realisation of a long-held ambition.

Taylor will aim to become a three-time undisputed world champion when she takes on Frenchwoman Flora Pili in Dublin.

The 40-year-old, who has won 25 professional fights and avenged her only defeat against Chantelle Cameron, will defend her light-welterweight WBO, WBA and IBF titles against Pili, who boasts an unbeaten 12-0 record.

With the vacant WBC title on the line, the Bray fighter has finally got her dream of boxing in front of a packed crowd at the Dublin venue.

But much focus will also centre on Irving, who regards taking charge of the contest as "right up there" with any of his previous assignments during more than 30 years as a referee.

"I can't believe that on Saturday night I'm going to be refereeing the biggest fight Ireland has ever seen. That is just amazing to try and understand," he told BBC Sport NI.

"It's an amazing honour to be recognised as an A-star referee, a world-class referee, to have people's confidence and support to referee such a big event.

"I'm thrilled, sometimes I still can't believe it. People come up to me and congratulate me and show me a lot of support.

"I've hoped that one day before I retire I would hopefully get a world title fight at home, with the WBC, and the dream has come true."

A former boxer himself with Holy Trinity in west Belfast, Irving's refereeing career has taken him around the globe, but being in charge of such a prestigious and historic fight in his native Ireland is a challenge that he is looking forward to hugely.

"I've been travelling the world since 2014 and I've always said I wish someone from Ireland would be up to that standard with the WBC," he added.

"I always said to myself wouldn't it be amazing to have someone that I could referee at home and lo and behold, Katie Taylor. She's an unbelievable ambassador for boxing and she opens herself up to everybody, not just in boxing.

"She has a great fanbase, she's a household name, north and south of Ireland, and to be part of that and to referee her I'm absolutely gobsmacked.

"In and out of the ring, she is such an icon."

Irving says he will go through a well established routine in his preparations for the big fight.

"A world title fight you make sure you have your uniform together, your pens, your scorecard, your towel and your water.

"You make sure you are hydrated because it could be a warm night and the fight could go the whole way, the whole 10 rounds, which can be very tiring.

"I'll be prepared, I always do a bit of training, always keep myself right eating wise.

"I can assure everyone that I'll be ready, no matter how big the fight is, how big of an occasion it will be, I'll be ready. I'm just looking forward to getting in there and I just hope it all goes according to plan."

The Belfast referee added that being prepared for all potential scenarios, including those that may not be anticipated, is all part of being fight-ready.

"It's the unexpected, being a referee. That part of me is always ready to go. That's where the confidence and the experience I have got now comes in, they have that confidence in me to make it an equal and smooth competition and may the best person win.

"You will be nervous, that's the thing about boxing, it's the unexpected.

"If you're a boxer, you go out to box, you have your programme in mind, you've done your work and you're ready to go.

"Refereeing is just the same. I've done my work, kept myself together, and do a lot of work, I do a lot of remote scoring, keep myself sharp, looking for the unexpected, and to be as quick as I can for the unexpected."

articles.title: UFC: Michael 'Venom' Page fights last UFC bout on contract in Paris
articles.summary: Michael 'Venom' Page says he needs to remind the UFC why they signed him, with his contract set to end after his UFC Paris bout on Saturday.
articles.body:
Michael 'Venom' Page will fight the final bout on his UFC contract when he takes on Nursulton Ruziboev in Paris on Saturday.

The 39-year-old has had a mixed career in the octagon since joining in 2024, with four wins from five fights - and all his victories by decision.

Known for his eye-catching striking, MVP admits he has underperformed in his UFC tenure without a stoppage to his name.

"I'm still buzzing to be in this game, but then there's also [the fact] I feel like I haven't delivered what I wanted to deliver," Page said.

"We (Page and the UFC) don't seem to be as aligned as I thought we would be.

"Maybe at the beginning I felt like we were - something's changed. But either way, the goal is [to] keep stepping out there and kicking people in the face.

"[This fight is to] specifically to remind the UFC why they brought me to this organisation."

Page has openly spoken about his frustration about the frequency of his fights, questioning why the UFC were not booking him more regularly.

The Englishman has fought twice at middleweight – beating Sharabutdin Magomedov and Jared Cannonier - despite being a seasoned welterweight.

An all-British bout with Leon Edwards has also not materialised.

Page faces a tough opponent in Ruziboev, who arrived in the UFC in 2024 with 20 submissions, has competed in 50 MMA fights and has four stoppages in his five victories in the octagon, with one defeat.

Uzbekistan's Ruziboev, 32, is the underdog against the more experienced Page, who is back at middleweight again for this bout.

With Page set to enter free agency, he would represent an attractive option for several rival promotions having spent most of his MMA career with Bellator.

But the Londoner is keen to sit down with the UFC after Saturday.

"This fight is important to re-establish myself with the UFC," Page said.

"Then sit down with them and say 'OK, guys, can I have an idea of what you expect of me? Can I have an idea of what direction is best for me to work towards? Can I have an idea of what it is that you guys need from me?'

"And then we get to work... I prefer if I have targets, and I have an idea of what I'm supposed to do, then I go and attack it."

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili: Tears and tricolours - an inside look at Irish icon's final fight week
articles.summary: An inside look at Katie Taylor's emotional final fight week as 80,000 fans prepare to salute Ireland's boxing icon at Croke Park on Saturday.
articles.body:
Katie Taylor smiles as she sits down for her fight-week media commitments, but her eyes give her away.

On Saturday, she faces unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili at Croke Park, bringing down the curtain on a career that has gone from disguising herself as a boy in a sport that barred women, to Olympic gold and undisputed titles.

The weight of a lifetime in the ring is catching up with an Irish icon preparing to step away.

"I thought I was handling all the emotions until today," the 40-year-old tells BBC Sport.

Taylor's usual defensive armour is slipping as the reality of a Croke Park farewell sets in. There is no next opponent waiting in the shadows, only 80,000 roaring voices, a sea of green, white and orange tricolours and the final chapter of a transcendent career.

"This is the stuff of dreams and I'm pinching myself that it's happening," Taylor adds.

"I look back at my career and think how remarkable it has been. The highs, the lows, the failures, the disappointments and the successes."

Tears and laughter as Taylor shows a new side

Taylor has never hidden her disdain for the circus of fight-week theatre, preferring the sanctuary of the gym.

But this week she has welled up under the glare of the cameras and stayed a fraction longer during face-offs to absorb the magnitude of the moment.

"Every fighter in the world wishes they were in this position," she says.

"I'm just blown away from the support from this country. I don't think there are many other countries where 80,000 show up for a female athlete.

"The crowd - hearing 'ole ole ole' one last time - feeling the atmosphere, seeing the tricolours all over the place..."

The emotion has rippled through her inner circle. Eddie Hearn choked up mid-sentence during the final news conference when it dawned on him this was the last time he would experience a Taylor fight week.

"When it's all said and done you will look at your belts, you might look at your bank balance. But you will sit there, close your eyes and recall all those incredible moments in your life that made you cry," he later told BBC Sport.

"I will cry on the ring walk. I will cry in the [post-fight] interview."

Taylor is softly spoken and laser-focused, but this week has unlocked a relaxed side of her rarely seen by the public. She joked during final media commitments about flipping the table just to disrupt the monotony.

"Katie Taylor is one of the funniest people I've met. Unexpectedly funny. She's so strong and determined. But people who know, she's very jovial, she's got great energy and I think she's soaking all that up," Hearn adds.

'Dear Katie, how far we have come...' - Taylor gets reply from her hero

Five moments that shaped Taylor's legendary career

Ali 'The Greatest' but Maguire the latest to win in Croke Park

How a bus tour led to a national celebration

All week, her nearest and dearest have insisted she is Ireland's greatest ever sportsperson. Manager Brian Peters jokingly issued an apology to Roy Keane, reassuring him he was a close second.

From taxi drivers gridlocked in traffic to those pulling pints in Temple Bar, everyone across the capital is frantically seeking spare tickets.

But even with Taylor's popularity, selling out Croke Park is no easy feat. While she has a reputation for being fiercely zoned into her training rather than chasing the spotlight, she has put work into the promotion. And perhaps even enjoyed it.

Peters spearheaded an exhausting, 1,500-mile island-wide bus tour spanning all 32 counties, completing dozens of radio chats and community stops to promote the swansong.

Coverage on Radio 5 Sports Extra from 19:00 BST, then 5 Live from 22:00. Ringwalks for main event expected between 22:00 and 22:30.

"No-one works as hard as Katie," Peters says. "Those four days she did not stop working. These stadiums don't sell out on their own."

When thousands mobbed the gates at a Kilkenny stop on an unforgiving timetable, Taylor refused to turn a blind eye. "Ah Brian, we can't drive past them," Peters recalls Taylor insisting, pulling the vehicle over to take group photos.

That effort has helped turn Saturday into something bigger than a boxing event. About 80% of those inside Croke Park will be attending a live fight for the first time, while 65% of tickets were sold outside Dublin.

With the bout also being shown on free-to-air TV across Ireland, Taylor's farewell - which will include music from one of the nation's biggest pop groups, Westlife - has become a national celebration.

Taylor must 'keep emotions in check' for fairytale ending

At Wednesday's public workout, 10-year-old Clodagh Keating from Dublin was picked from the crowd to hug Taylor and join her for a few boxing drills.

Clodagh was in tears and overwhelmed by the moment. "I'd do anything for Katie Taylor. I'd even sell my dog," she said afterwards.

Taylor says that if even one young girl in the stands falls in love with boxing because of her, every hard mile will have been worth it.

"Looking at all these opportunities these girls have now, it's remarkable. I'm so happy that you walk into any boxing gym and it's packed with female fighters. On a weekly basis, these amazing women headlining these huge shows. I love that," Taylor reflects.

"I'm so happy to see all these female fighters now don't have to go through the same opposition I went through. The same adversity I went through. When I look back on my journey, that will be my greatest legacy."

Yet beneath the emotional tributes and patriotic pageantry, a dangerous sporting test awaits.

Pili has spent the week quietly slipping through corridors while the media storm swirls around Taylor.

The undefeated challenger arrives with a 12-0 record and a hunger to create her own story.

"I have nothing to lose and everything to win," Pili, 29, said.

But with fight-week media commitments cleverly packed into the start of the week, Taylor has been given the space to get the tears and emotion out of her system.

"I don't think I can prepare for what happens on Saturday, but I'm going to try and keep emotions in check and try and enjoy the ringwalk. But the most important thing is to win," she says.

Asked how she will feel when the dust settles on Sunday morning, Taylor says: "Probably a bit relieved - I don't have to take any more punches again."

The tears may come again at the end of Saturday night. This time, though, the final bell really will mean the end.

articles.title: Justin Gaethje vs Conor McGregor to fight? Gaethje eyes showdown with Conor and wants to “shut him up”
articles.summary: International Sports News: Justin Gaethje has already gone through some of the biggest names in the UFC, but there’s apparently one more fight that could make sense for the fina.
articles.body: Justin Gaethje has already gone through some of the biggest names in the UFC, but there’s apparently one more fight that could make sense for the final stretch of his career. After becoming UFC lightweight champion in June, Gaethje has now pointed toward Conor McGregor as the opponent he would most want to face again. That choice is a little different from where Gaethje’s head was earlier this year. He had previously been thinking about getting another shot at Max Holloway or Charles Oliveira, two fighters he had lost to. But with Ilia Topuria defeating both of them, Gaethje feels he can put those revenge ideas aside. McGregor, instead, has become the fight he wants.Justin Gaethje said he isn't chasing revenge anymoreThe 37-year-old has spent the last nine years in the UFC building a reputation around his wild, high-pressure style. Victories over Tony Ferguson, Dustin Poirier and Topuria have added plenty to his résumé, but his willingness to embrace chaos is a huge part of why he has become such a popular figure.Now, though, his career is moving toward its final stage. Gaethje admitted that his time away from competition has been enjoyable, especially after making sacrifices earlier in the year.“Lots of traveling and lots of good food,” he said in an interview with UFC on YouTube, explaining that he had sacrificed family holidays while fighting in January and June. He joked that he now has “three Arizona trips coming up” to make up for that time.Being champion has also changed the way he looks at the division. Instead of chasing one particular fighter, Gaethje knows the best contenders are now chasing him.“There's always been a champion. I always had somebody to chase,” he said. Now, he simply has to defend what he has while waiting for upcoming fights to determine his next opponent.Why Conor McGregor is suddenly the pickThat leaves the interesting part. When asked who from his career he would choose to fight again, Gaethje initially had Holloway and Oliveira in mind.“Damn, there's really no one,” he said before explaining that Oliveira or Holloway would have been his choices previously. But Topuria's wins over both gave him a way to move on from those old losses.“So, I guess McGregor,” Gaethje said. And his reason was brutally simple. “Yeah. It'd be fun to shut him up.”That line gives the potential matchup a very different feel from the revenge fights Gaethje had considered earlier. He isn't saying he has a specific opponent lined up. In fact, he made it clear that he isn't currently focused on one name because the division's upcoming fights will help determine who gets the next opportunity.For now, Gaethje is enjoying his new position at the top. He has the lightweight title, contenders are coming after him, and his own preferred legacy fight is clear: Conor McGregor.Whether that matchup actually happens isn't established in the reference material. What is clear is that if Gaethje gets to choose one familiar name for another fight before his career ends, McGregor has moved to the front of his list.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaron McKenna: IBF champion set for world middleweight unification showdown with WBO title holder Denzel Bentley
articles.summary: IBF middleweight champion Aaron McKenna is expected to face WBO champion Denzel Bentley in a unification clash before the end of 2026; McKenna extended his 100 per cent pro record with a hometown win over Etinosa Oliha in Dublin
articles.body:
McKenna claimed the IBF belt with an impressive points win over Etinosa Oliha last month in Dublin and could soon have an opportunity to add another world title.

Bentley was elevated to WBO champion in July after Janibek Alimkhanuly relinquished the belt.

The Londoner had previously beaten Endry Saavedra to become WBO interim champion in April.

Speaking after his world title win, McKenna vowed to dominate the division.

"I've said it before and I'll say it again I will literally fight anyone out there. I just want to unify, whatever it takes, prove I'm the best in the world. That's the sport of boxing. You look back in the day, the 80s and 90s, they all fought each other," McKenna said.

"And this is exactly why Zuffa Boxing's going to be the future. It's already taking over. Everybody's fighting each other, there's no more hiding."

Before beating Oliha, McKenna told Sky Sports about his intention to "clean up" the division, go undisputed and eventually finish his career as a heavyweight.

"I'm 6ft 3in now and I have a very long reach as well. My body's the type of body that could fill out easily enough as well weight-wise," McKenna told Sky Sports . "Once I'm done at 160lb, take over 168 and then 175. But by the time I finish out, I plan to have at least one fight at heavyweight.

"The last two big fighters in it [middleweight division] were Canelo and GGG [Gennady Golovkin], so I kind of want to bring big-time boxing in the middleweight division and bring it back to life. [Bentley] would be another good fight."

One of the most unheralded, and shortest duration, heavyweight champions in boxing history returns to the ring Friday night after a 25-month hiatus.

Andy Ruiz Jr.. who upset Anthony Joshua in "AJ's" U.S. debut in 2019 but lost a return bout six months later, is back in business to try and stake a claim to elite status in a fractured big-man division.

The division's four significant championship belts were tossed into oblivion when undisputed champ Oleksandr Usyk vacated his claims. And though they've all since been awarded, Ruiz is still seeking to reclaim a piece of what once was his.

He'll face once-beaten Polish export Damian Knyba in a scheduled 12-rounder atop a four-bout main card at the Prudential Center in Newark, N.J. that'll be streamed on DAZN.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Eddie Hearn says talks have 'reopened' to stage British heavyweight blockbuster at Wembley Stadium
articles.summary: A long-awaited blockbuster fight between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury has been stuck in negotiations in recent months amid an apparent disagreement over the location for the event, Joshua's team having remained insistent it must take place in the United Kingdom
articles.body:
Negotiations for the Fury vs Joshua fight had hit a major stumbling block after Madison Square Garden in New York emerged as the preferred venue to stage the blockbuster bout.

But Hearn has released a statement on social media, revealing that Wembley is again being considered as the venue for the fight.

He wrote: "I want to thank everyone for the unbelievable support!"

"You have been heard and talks have now re-opened for Wembley.

"Let's make history with one of the biggest sporting moments [British flag] has ever seen."

Sky Sports has contacted Fury's promoter Frank Warren for a response.

Speaking on DAZN, Hearn added that he had spoken to Mayor of London Sadiq Khan regarding bringing the fight to Wembley.

"I spoke to Sadiq Khan today, there's a narrative going around that Netflix want the fight to accommodate the American audience a little bit later. I get that, so we could do the fight later in Britain, but everybody is saying 'you can't do that, there's a curfew at Wembley'. Sadiq Khan has come back and said 'woah guys, we'll move heaven and earth to get this fight in London'," said Hearn.

Fury had taken to social media earlier this week to label Joshua a "coward" while insisting he had been "conning" boxing fans amid the continued hold up.

Mayor of London Khan spoke to Sky Sports on Thursday evening, urging Fury and Joshua's promoters to "get the fight to London".

"I understand the temptation of going to Madison Square Garden," Khan told Sky Sports News . "I understand the temptation of the money and offer, but the fans are here.

"We've been loyal to Tyson and to Anthony. We love them both, and we'd love to see them boxing here in London.

"I'm positive Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua know how much we love both of them. I'm not sure how much the promoters know how much we love both of them, but my message to the promoters is why don't you do what Tyson and Anthony want, which is get the fight in London.

"We'll get 100,000 people watching them live, plus millions watching across the globe fighting amongst the fans who've loved them from the beginning."

Khan also revealed he had been in direct contact with Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn, saying the Matchroom chairman had approached him for help with organising the fight:

"We've hosted some of the biggest boxing events in history in London during my mayoralty.

"Many British fans are fans of Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Many Londoners love both Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Both Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua recognise the importance of British boxing fans.

"The promoters know we're here to help. We've approached those in the know to say we're here to help.

"Eddie Hearn has approached us and we're keen to work with Eddie and the team."

Joshua warmed up for the Fury fight with a second-round knockout victory over Kristian Prenga in July, but he was floored twice in the first round.

Fury also last fought in July as he sealed a seventh-round stoppage win over Mariusz Wach.

articles.summary: El peleador checheno da por hecho que Nassourdine Imavov será el siguiente retador al cinturón de la UFC, por lo que ya tiene otro nombre en mente
articles.body: El pasado UFC 329, Khamzat Chimaev perdió el invicto y el cinturón de peso medio tras caer contra Sean Strickland por decisión unánime en una de las mayores sorpresas del año. El peleador checheno no pudo dominar al estadounidense en el suelo y acabo sucumbiendo por su falta de cardio y su inferioridad en el striking, aunque se ha tirado los últimos meses pidiendo a la UFC una revancha. Sin embargo, a día de hoy ya da por hecho que tendrá que volver a ganarse la oportunidad titular, por lo que ya tiene otro rival en mente. El combate entre Chimaev y Strickland fue uno de los más mediáticos del año, ya que ambos parecían tener un beef personal que finalmente resultó ser puro teatro. Esto no gustó nada a la UFC, ya que el resultado fue muy ficticio y la gente quedó decepcionada tanto con la pelea como con una rivalidad que no fue real. Al no haber realizado ni una sola defensa de cinturón, Chimaev tendrá que volver a ganarse la pelea por el cinturón, y para ello quiere enfrentarse a Caio Borralho. El peleador de los 'Fighting Nerds' viene de ganar a Reinier De Ridder el pasado marzo, y tiene un récord de ocho victorias y una derrota en la UFC. Por tanto, es el rival idóneo para que 'Borz' recupere la confianza perdida y se decida quién sera el siguiente contendiente al título. Así lo hizo saber Khamzat con un simple tuit en el que escribía 'Caio' junto a un emoticono. La única derrota de Borralho en la UFC fue precisamente hace un año ante Nassourdine Imavov, que todo hace indicar que será el próximo rival de Sean Strickland. El peleador galo viene de noquear a Israel Adesanya y de dominar a Caio, por lo que tendrá la oportunidad de ser campeón ante Sean en una pelea que será una revancha del combate que tuvieron ambos en 2023 y que se llevó el estadounidense por decisión -última derrota de Imavov en la UFC-. A pesar de que en un principio Chimaev estaba convencido de que la UFC le daría la revancha, ha acabado aceptando su destino, e incluso ha hablado acerca de que sea Imavov el próximo contendiente al cinturón. "No hay sorpresa. ¿Cuánto tiempo ha estado esperando Imavov ahora? Ya es el contendiente. Quien gane, lo tomaremos", afirmó en unas declaraciones a Ushatayka. De hecho, había rumores de que el peleador checheno subiría directamente a peso semipesado por lo duro que fue su corte de peso en la pelea contra Strickland, pero ha habido cambio de planes. Hasta que no vuelva a obtener el título y arrase con la división, Khamzat ha revelado que no subirá de categoría para buscar ser doble campeón, por lo que todavía tiene cuentas pendientes en 185 libras para demostrar que esa derrota no le ha afectado lo más mínimo.

articles.title: Reaparece Ilia Topuria: "En la vida no siempre se gana. Y no pasa nada"
articles.standfirst: El 'Matador' vuelve a escena casi tres meses después de su derrota en UFC Casa Blanca con una emotiva e íntima carta a su hijo Hugo
articles.summary: El 'Matador' vuelve a escena casi tres meses después de su derrota en UFC Casa Blanca con una emotiva e íntima carta a su hijo Hugo
articles.body: El pasado 14 de junio, en el jardín sur de la Casa Blanca, Ilia Topuria perdió ante Justin Gaethje. Cedió la corona de campeón del peso ligero de la UFC y sufrió su primera derrota como peleador profesional. A escasos metros del octágono, sentado entre familiares, equipo y amigos, estaba su hijo Hugo, de cinco años. Es a él al que el ‘Matador’ le escribe esta carta, sus primeras palabras casi tres meses después de aquella noche en Washington D.C. Este es el contenido de dicha carta: “Hugo... Llevo unos días pensando en ti. En lo que sentiste cuando me viste caer. Sé que sufriste y, como padre, daría cualquier cosa por haberte ahorrado ese momento. Pero también me alegra que lo hayamos vivido juntos. Porque aquel día nos hizo más fuertes a los dos. Quiero que recuerdes siempre una cosa: en la vida no siempre se gana. Y no pasa nada. Porque perder no es lo importante. Lo importante es cómo pierdes. Quién decides ser cuando todo se pone oscuro. Cuando tienes que elegir entre quedarte en el suelo... o volver a levantarte. Creo que Dios quiso que viviera ese momento para enseñarme una lección que ninguna victoria podía enseñarme. Que el carácter no aparece cuando todo va bien; se revela cuando la vida te pone delante de su día más difícil. ¿Y sabes qué descubrí? Que después de visitar ese infierno, soy más fuerte que antes. Porque un campeón no es el que nunca cae. Es el que siempre encuentra un motivo para levantarse. Eso es lo único que deseo para ti. No que ganes siempre, sino que nunca tengas miedo de perder. Que ninguna derrota tenga el poder de decirte quién eres. Porque eso solo lo decides tú. Y, pase lo que pase, recuerda siempre esto: el carácter es la única victoria que nadie puede quitarte”. Es la primera aparición pública de un Topuria que ha dedicado el verano a sanar cuerpo y mente. Aún, pese a los rumores que señalan diciembre como fecha de regreso, es pronto para pensar en una próxima vuelta a la jaula.

articles.title: UFC Fight Night 287: Dan Hooker vs. Salahdine Parnasse expert pick
articles.summary: Salahdine Parnasse debuts in a headlining spot on home soil against Dan Hooker. MMA Junkie fight analyst Dan Tom breaks down the UFC Paris main event.
articles.body:
MMA Junkie analyst Dan Tom goes in depth to break down the biggest fights in the UFC. Today, he takes a closer look at UFC Fight Night 287's main event between Dan Hooker and Salahdine Parnasse.

Height : 6'0" Age : 36 Weight : 155 lbs. Reach : 75"

Last fight : TKO loss to Benoit St. Denis (Jan. 31, 2026)

Stance/striking style : Orthodox/muay Thai

Salahdine Parnasse UFC Fight Night 287 preview

Height : 5'10" Age : 28 Weight : 155 lbs. Reach : 73"

Last fight : TKO win over Kenneth Cross (May 16, 2026)

Stance/striking style : Southpaw/kickboxing

+ KSW lightweight and featherweight title

+ Pro boxing exp. (1-0 with 1 win by KO)

Dan Hooker vs. Salahdine Parnasse point of interest: Open-stance affair

The main event in Paris features a lightweight showdown between UFC stalwart Dan Hooker and promotional debutant Salahdine Parnasse.

Parnasse is a fighter whom I've had on my radar for years (featured in my 2023 prospect to watch column), so it's nice to see him finally onboarded by the world leader.

A flexible French prospect, I tend to describe Parnasse as a more active and boxing-heavy version of Leon Edwards.

Operating out of a southpaw stance with similar swagger, Parnasse is a fairly active jabber and feinter – utilizing said tactics to set up the bigger shots to come. From pulling out opportunities for cross counters to setting up hard Thai kicks from the rear, Parnasse possesses all the weapons that a southpaw should never leave home without.

Parnasse will even attack the rear legs of orthodox opposition with Sittichai Sitsongpeenong-style kicks, but the Frenchman will need to be mindful in those ranges against a long, lanky striker like Hooker.

A muay Thai stylist who can work with all forms of pressure, Hooker wields a diverse arsenal of attacks.

Whether he's fighting from orthodox or southpaw, the New Zealand native can strike well from either stance, both coming forward and off the counter.

Working nicely off a long, well-placed jab, Hooker can prod with effect or attach it to the end of combinations as a disruptive check to help dissuade counters. Often following up with his patented crosses and head kicks, the 36-year-old talent will continue to vary his tempo and attacks throughout the contest, attempting to build pace and pressure.

Helping glue together Hooker's offensive repertoire is his ability to effectively feint in space – something that I suspect he can thank Eugene Bareman and the City Kickboxing crew for. Nevertheless, despite Hooker's noted technical improvements and inherent toughness, defense has not necessarily been his strong suit, making offense a potent, two-way street in this fight.

Dan Hooker vs. Salahdine Parnasse point of interest: Potential grappling threats

Considering where Hooker has lost his last two fights, no one should be shocked if Parnasse opts for the path of least resistance this Saturday.

Akin to the Edwards comparison in the previous section, Parnasse is a fighter who is not afraid to take things to the floor when needed.

Whether Parnasse is hitting reactive shots on opponents who come in hot or is countering offense in the clinch with takedowns of his own, he has proven to be someone who will happily take what's given to him and will not force things out of ego. Parnasse is a vicious bodworker in tight, but is just as happy to hit shuck-bys or go for tactics like Alexandre Pantoja-like back takes off of crab ride sits.

That said, Hooker also does some of his best work in close quarters, demonstrating some underrated wrestling in the latter stages of his UFC tenure.

Perhaps it's his experience with muay Thai, but Hooker comports himself well in clinch scenarios, seldom being stuck against the fence for long before showing some type of ability to spin his opposition around, as well as occasionally looking for takedowns of his own.

Improving his scrambling in recent years, Hooker shows a solid awareness of his hips and an ability to snatch backs in transit that has served him well. When an opponent gets too overzealous in going for a takedown, Hooker puts his long arms to good use as he gets creative with his front-choke threats.

Parnasse has shown solid submission defense and positional awareness against credible opposition on the KSW scene, but he'll still need to be on his best behavior when tying up with a crafty veteran like Hooker.

The oddsmakers and the public heavily favor the UFC newcomer, listing Parnasse -700 and Hooker +440 via FanDuel.

Dan Hooker vs. Salahdine Parnasse prediction, pick

Although these odds are almost insultingly wide given the upsets we've seen lately, I can't disagree with who is favored.

Don't get me wrong, Hooker absolutely has all the tools for an upset here, so no one should be acting like the world is falling apart if Parnasse is the one who gets caught with a head kick or a left hand in the heat of things. However, given how high I've been on Parnasse's game, I have a hard time picking against the Frenchman in this spot.

Aside from left-sided strikes and Parnasse's general shot selections being traditional trouble spots for Hooker, "The Hangman" also has a propensity to push action into the clinch when he doesn't need to (a mistake that led to him getting finished in his last two fights).

Against a fighter like Parnasse, who feels at home both striking and wrestling in said spaces, Hooker could find himself, once again, playing with some serious fire.

Parnasse may not be a standout grappler from a resume or on-paper accolade perspective, but countering and coming out on top of grappling scenarios has been a quiet specialty of the former two-division KSW champion for some time now. Add in Parnasse's predilection for punishing the body and legs, and I can't help but side with the fighter with 14 title fights to find a finish in the early-to-middle rounds.

The official pick is for Parnasse to spark off a stoppage via bodywork by the end of Round 2.

Prediction: Parnasse inside the distance

Dan Hooker vs. Salahdine Parnasse start time, how to watch

As the main event, Hooker and Parnasse are expected to make their walks to the octagon at approximately 5:35 p.m. ET. The fight streams on Paramount+ .
