articles.title: One fight left on UFC deal, but Michael Page knows his title route: ‘It's gonna be middleweight’
articles.summary: MMA News: Two-and-a-half years into his UFC career, Michael ‘Venom’ Page is down to the last fight of his original six-fight deal. The 39-year-old has won four .
articles.body: Two-and-a-half years into his UFC career, Michael ‘Venom’ Page is down to the last fight of his original six-fight deal. The 39-year-old has won four of five, fought at two weight classes and is now back at middleweight, where he says he sees his route to a UFC title.For all the changes, Page feels his UFC run has not built the momentum he expected. The loss to Ian Machado Garry at welterweight was followed by wins over Shara Magomedov and former middleweight title challenger Jared Cannonier, but his return to 170 pounds for Sam Patterson did not lead to the run of fights he had hoped for.“I feel like I had momentum, and it slowed down,” Page told TimesofIndia.com ahead of his middleweight fight against Nursulton Ruziboev at UFC Fight Night in Paris. “So this fight is to restart that momentum again, and build towards the top.”Page looks to restart his momentum at 185Page's move between the divisions has been tied to that search for momentum. After his wins at middleweight, he wanted to return to welterweight because he saw fights there that interested him. But, he said, getting opponents to agree to those fights became difficult.“I wanted to go back to welterweight, just because I feel like there’s some really exciting fights at welterweight,” Page said. “But the guys at welterweight don't like to fight regularly enough for me, and I wasn't getting enough people saying yes to wanting to fight me, so it made more sense to go to middleweight, because I feel like I'll have regular fights.”That brought him back to 185 pounds, where Page now says the title route is clear.“Well, I've solidified myself now at middleweight, so it's gonna be middleweight,” he said when asked which division he sees himself fighting for a UFC title in.The move up has also suited him physically. Page said he feels stronger at middleweight without losing the speed that has been one of the defining parts of his game.“They gave me more food,” Page said with a chuckle. “To eat more, and feel a lot stronger. So yeah, I definitely feel stronger. I equally still feel as fast, but I feel a lot faster than the guys at middleweight, just because I'm used to exploding and keeping up with welterweights. So the middleweights, I feel my speed is even better there.”Ruziboev brings a different test for PageThe next step is Ruziboev, who is ranked No. 15 at middleweight and comes into Paris on a three-fight UFC winning streak. The Uzbek is 5-0 in the division, with his only UFC defeat coming in his lone appearance at welterweight.His most recent win was another reminder of the danger he carries on the ground. Ruziboev submitted Andrey Pulyaev in the first round in June, taking his career total to 21 submission wins, according to his UFC record.Page is not expecting to be able to switch off that part of the fight.“Yeah, I think he's a long, rangy fighter. And as you say, he's got very good submissions, so that's definitely his dangerous area,” Page said. “So yeah, it's making sure I don't get caught up in anything where he can use that advantage against me. If we're on the ground, it's because I've gone for the takedown, or I've taken him down, and not the other way around. Can't let him take my back, you know, I have to just be vigilant in the grappling area, and then do exactly what I do well in the striking area.”Ruziboev's run at middleweight has been one of the more consistent parts of his UFC career. After his brief move to welterweight, he returned to 185 pounds and has won three straight, including the Pulyaev submission.One fight left, and a title route in mindFor Page, though, the opponent is only part of what makes Saturday important. It is his last fight on the current UFC contract, and he has been open about wanting a new deal - provided it gives him a clearer route towards the bigger fights and, eventually, the title.He has previously described the difficulty of getting a Top-10 opponent as frustrating, saying he had been looking for bigger names over his previous three fights. But Page does not want the contract situation to bleed into fight night.“Yeah, like I said, just having interviews and speaking about it is just what it is. I don't… after the interview's finished, I don't think about it,” he said. “The only thought is Saturday, making sure my fight's good, and making sure I feel the best, and I go out there and just put on a performance.”That performance could also answer a question that has followed the Bellator standout through his UFC run. He arrived in the promotion known for spectacular finishes, but all five of his UFC fights so far have gone to the judges. His last three - against Cannonier, Patterson and Ruziboev - have come after the move into the middleweight picture.At 39, Page knows the window is not getting wider. What he wants now is a run that moves quickly enough to matter. For the next six months, at least, there will be plenty happening outside the cage too. Page said he has acting work and auditions alongside his training.“It looks… it looks very, very busy, because I'm not only gonna be fighting, but I'm doing some acting stuff as well, so it's gonna be very, very busy, but it still looks like a lot of training, and… and now a lot of auditions.”(Watch UFC Fight Night - Hooker vs Parnasse on September 06, 2026, from 12:30 AM IST live on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD, Sony Sports Ten 3 SD & HD (Hindi), Sony Sports Ten 4 SD (Tamil,Telugu, Kannada) & Sony LIV.)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili: Sun shines as fighters weigh in at Trinity College
articles.summary: Katie Taylor and Flora Pili weigh in under the light-welterweight limit at a sun-kissed Trinity College in Dublin before they fight for the undisputed title at Croke Park on Saturday.
articles.body:
Katie Taylor has taken her final week as a professional boxer in her stride.

Each media event has been ticked off with the kind of composure and poise she has displayed in the ring for over two decades.

Dublin blessed Taylor and opponent Flora Pili with some early autumn sun as they weighed in at Trinity College before Saturday's undisputed light-welterweight battle at a sold-out Croke Park.

Taylor has not missed weight once in her 26-fight career and she was not going to buck the trend as she was greeted by adoring fans - many whom have followed her career since she won Olympic gold in 2012.

The announcement of the weights - both coming in just under the 10st (63.5kg) limit - was almost immaterial.

All 80,000 tickets for Saturday's undisputed light-welterweight fight have been long snapped up and demand for Friday's ceremonial weigh-in proved just as high.

Supporters packed into Trinity College, a seat of higher learning founded in 1592 by Queen Elizabeth I, to catch a glimpse of the queen of Irish sport.

Women were not permitted to study at Trinity College until 1904 but Taylor, who has smashed barriers for women in and out of the ring - was the star attraction.

Trinity's old library is an attraction in its own right, home to the Book of Kells - an illustrated manuscript, which contains the four Gospels of the New Testament in Latin - but those in its grounds were there for their own piece of history on this final fight week of Taylor's illustrious career.

The 40-year-old, two-weight undisputed champion, may not be a huge fan of the fight week obligations and making weight is certainly an aspect to the sport that will not be missed, but this was an opportunity to soak it all in one last time.

Pili has been the perfect guest all week, complimentary and polite, but the Frenchwoman is not here to be a tourist and there was an air of confidence as she hit the scales.

The 29-year-old has stitched together a perfect record of 12 wins and has an opportunity to raise her own reputation if she can pull of a major upset.

It is Pili's biggest night, an opportunity to catapult herself into the upper echelons of the fight game, but an also occasion she has never experienced and looked a little bemused as she stepped on to the scales.

As violinists played Irish folk song 'Óró, sé do bheatha 'bhaile' [Óró - you are welcome home], Taylor appeared to a rapturous reception and the fighters went through the formalities, all smiles and handshakes.

Tears and tricolours - inside Irish icon Taylor's final fight week

'Dear Katie, how far we have come...' - Taylor gets reply from her hero

Five moments that shaped Taylor's legendary career

Taylor rarely displays emotion in fight week but she has shown a different side of the past couple of days as the curtain starts to fall on her illustrious career.

The Bray fighter, who had her mother Bridgit close by, choked up at times and appeared as she delivered her final messages.

"I'm so excited. I've been saying all week how I grateful I am for this opportunity. I've been dreaming of this for the last few years and now it's just one day away. It's just one day away from ending my career in my dream venue of Croke Park," Taylor told the crowd after her final face-off.

"All these amazing people are here today and I'm blown away. I can't wait to step in there and I want to put in a performance worthy of everyone's support.

"You have carried me through the Rio Olympics, London Olympics and throughout my professional career. Thank you."

Both fighters can now breathe a little easier as it is onto the task at hand.

The buzz that has steadily built all week will reach a crescendo when they make their way to the ring around 22:00 BST on Saturday, and while the occasion remains grand, the destination of the title belts remains the priority.

"My mind is very much focused on the fight," Taylor reiterated.

"I have a tough challenger in front of me but I've built a reputation of taking tough fights - why treat my last fight any differently?

"Tomorrow is going to be an amazing celebration. I'm super proud to represent this amazing country. Let's go one more time."

Coverage on Radio 5 Sports Extra from 19:00 BST, then 5 Live from 22:00. Ringwalks for main event expected between 22:00 and 22:30.

articles.title: Katie Taylor ready to go 'one more time' as glittering career ends at Croke Park with dreams of being undisputed again
articles.summary: Katie Taylor weight in at 139.6lbs for her final fight - an undisputed super-lightweight showdown against unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili in Dublin on Saturday night, in front of 80,000 fans - "I want to put on a performance worthy of the support I have had these last few years"
articles.body:
Taylor will aim to retire as a three-time undisputed world champion when she takes on unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park in Dublin.

The 40-year-old, who weighed in at 139.6lbs for the super-lightweight showdown compared to Pili's 139.9lbs, done it all in boxing.

Her accolades including winning Olympic gold in London in 2012 and, along with Amanda Serrano, becoming the first woman to headline a fight card at New York's iconic Madison Square ‌Garden.

She also avenged her sole pro defeat, against Chantelle Cameron.

But she has never fought at Croke Park before - until now.

'This is what I was born for, this is what I was made for'

While fight week, quite rightly, has seen the great and good of boxing and beyond praise Taylor's career, hail the inspiration she has been and discuss the legacy she will leave, the woman herself is not looking beyond Pili.

Speaking shortly after hitting the scales on Friday evening, the Bray Bomber, said: "My mind is focused on the fight. I have a job to do against a very tough challenger.

"I have built my reputation on always taking the tough fights, so why treat my last fight any differently? This is what I was born for, this is what I was made for. Let's go one more time."

Taylor did, though, turn to address her fans at the weigh-in, many of whom will also be rooting for her inside the stadium this weekend.

"I am blown away. I want to put on a performance worthy of the support I have had these last few years

"You guys have carried me throughout the Olympics and my whole career. Thank you so much. I am so grateful.

"I am so excited. I have been dreaming about this for the last few years and I am one day away from ending my career in a dream venue in front of all these amazing people."

'Katie is an absolute hero to so many people'

Former world champion Carl Frampton, speaking on DAZN , feels the lure of a bout at Saturday's prolonged Taylor's time as an active fighter.

He said: "She has completed the sport but I think one of the reasons she held on was the dream of fighting at Croke Park. She has finally got it.

"Katie is an absolute hero to so many people, an inspiration. It is a perfect way to finish - but she has to win first and we can't rule out Pili who is a very good fighter."

Three-weight world champion Mikaela Mayer added: "Katie has always been very true to her word.

"If she says this is her last fight, I believe it to be. If she wants to come back, I would not be upset about it. We'd love to see her again.

"I am benefitting off of her hard work and everything she has helped create for the women in this sport. I am sad as I had always hoped to share the ring with Katie."

articles.title: BOOM! UFC Signs Croatia’s ‘Robocop’
articles.summary: The UFC Welterweight division just got even more exciting. According to a first report from Pelunaton, Roberto Soldic has officially signed with the UFC and...
articles.body:
The UFC Welterweight division just got even more exciting.

According to a first report from Pelunaton , Roberto Soldic has officially signed with the UFC and will be competing at 170 pounds. Croatia's "Robocop" may not be a household name in the US, but the ferocious knockout artist is a highly accomplished finisher. 21-4 overall, the former KSW double champion has finished 18 of his foes via knockout. Per the same source, Soldic is rumored (but not confirmed) to debut at UFC 334 on Nov. 14 in New York against an elite opponent.

Those who don't know Soldic are in for a treat. During his KSW run, Soldic split a pair of bouts with former UFC Middleweight champion Dricus du Plessis , as both men knocked out the other once . In 2022, Soldic signed with One Championship, but his career there didn't go as planned. In three fights spread across four years, Soldic suffered a gruesome nut shot , was knocked cold in a massive upset, and then scored his own brutal finish to leave the company on a victory.

It's great to see another high-profile signing straight to the UFC roster. A large majority of new signees join the promotion via Contender Series or as short-notice replacements, but an accomplished killer like Soldic deserves the respect and money that comes with a more direct contract.

Who should Soldic face in his debut? A fellow knockout artist like Uros Medic could make for a dynamic introduction to UFC fans.
